events.detail: 00-spec.yaml declares risk: medium and quorum analyze risk-score calculated medium (file_count_high: 13). No divergence event emitted; 00-spec.yaml was not modified.

hsme-cli search-fuzzy --project hexcell returned 3 low-similarity memories (top score 0.016). Advisory only per ADR 0008. Memory 1332 (HEX-013) was the sole relevant carry-over: an HTTP client built without a whole-request deadline can hang forever on a peer that completes TLS then goes silent. Recorded as a blueprint risk and encoded in the contract as a timeout wrapping connect, handshake, request and body read.
.ai/tasks/failed/ is empty, so quorum analyze failure-lookup returned null and contributed no prior-failure lessons to the risks array.
quorum analyze blueprint-context returned the seed set unchanged; affected_files was finalized from direct inspection of the workspace instead.

Cargo.lock at bfe5bb2 ships no TLS crate whatsoever. In a scratch crate on rustc 1.92.0, hyper 1.11 client + hyper-util 0.1 client-legacy + hyper-rustls 0.27 + rustls 0.23 (ring, default-features=false) + webpki-roots 1.0 both resolved and compiled clean, adding ~18 non-Windows crates. reqwest 0.12 resolved to a 132-package lock (~85 extra crates) and was rejected. hyper-rustls 0.28 does not exist; 0.27 is the current series.

A std::net::TcpListener fake server in a std thread drove the real client through 200-with-usage, 429 and stall-past-deadline cases with zero new dev-dependencies. Two findings encoded in the contract: the connector must use https_or_http() rather than https_only() for tests to reach loopback, and Content-Length must be computed from the body (a hand-counted literal produced hyper IncompleteBody).

The fifth verify command's regex was run against the exact rustls/hyper builder code the contract prescribes and produced no false positives; underscore being a word character keeps with_tls_config, with_root_certificates and builder_with_provider from matching \bwith\b.

docs/STATUS.md carries a HEX-007 pending decision assigned to stage A-4: the real provider needs a maximum call time comfortably under LIMITE_DE_DRENAJE_POR_DEFECTO (10 s, against the PRD's 30 s grace), because the drain limit is checked between events and not around one in flight. The contract resolves it with a 4000 ms default timeout, 1 default retry and a load-time cross-check that timeout*(1+reintentos) < limite_de_drenaje.

docs/adr/adr-0012-inferencia-externa.md does not exist on disk although docs/adr/README.md reserves the number with status 'Tomada en el PRD, por formalizar'. Because this task is the stage-A-4 work that makes external inference real, the contract formalizes adr-0012 here and flips only that row's status cell, without renumbering.
